object_description: extremely compact, cube-like school volume closing off the square
design_condition: the cube closes off the square and frees a large open space at ground level opposite the tall neighbouring buildings, with the footbridge forming the eastern wall of that space

positive: The compact cube closes off the square and creates a large open space as a counterpart to the square to the south
The footbridge becomes an independent building forming the wall of the all-weather square on the east side
Its location at street level lets the large open space be used for play and recreation beyond school hours
The concrete grid with light exposed brick parapets echoes the elegance of familiar industrial buildings
The clear structure finds its counterpart inside, with uses neatly stacked horizontally
A break terrace on the second floor allows a second entrance and separate access outside school hours
The kindergarten on the top floor has its own high-quality, directly accessible outdoor area
The neutral spatial structure based on small units ensures flexibility of room sizes within the skeleton construction
The compact building and the ground-level, non-underground pitch promise an economical realisation
The photovoltaic system on the roof is sufficient and the retention is well solved
A surprisingly simple, pragmatic and functional concept
negative: The open space is not a square in the classic sense, as most of it is occupied by the too-small all-weather pitch
The required fence is unsatisfactory in urban terms, as the pitch is neither a space nor a body
The beautiful gesture of the open staircase is lost with the fence
The concrete grid of the facade merely repeats what is already there
The building blends seamlessly into the surrounding new buildings and is very subordinate as a public building
The public ground floor uses are only accessed via the school entrance, with no use independent of school operations
Classrooms form double clusters instead of the favoured single clusters
Exclusively internal access far from street level will make the stairwell cramped at peak times
The reduced volume comes at the price of scarce and insufficiently daylit circulation areas
There is no sense of collective space
The ensemble of a small building and a fenced ground-level pitch is not strong enough to form an important public space
